intent: Group a Tabs root's triggers into one row (or column) and draw the indicator that marks which one is active.
typical_uses: The single row (or column) of triggers that sits above, or beside, a Tabs root's panels

dont_use_when.situation: A segmented, bordered row of mutually exclusive options with no panel to show per choice

instead.note: TabsList draws only its own filled-track or trackless-line looks; the bordered segmented-control look belongs to ToggleGroup, not to a Tabs variant.

invariants.text: TabsList's `variant` and `size` govern every TabsTrigger inside it; a trigger takes no prop of its own for either axis, so a list cannot hold two triggers that disagree.

anti_patterns.dont: Style a TabsList to look like a bordered segmented control
anti_patterns.do_instead: Reach for ToggleGroup - the segmented look is its variant, not a Tabs one

a11y.by: Base UI's Tabs.List - tablist role and roving-tabindex arrow-key navigation between triggers - exercised by tabs.test.tsx's "keeps a disabled tab reachable by arrow-key navigation without activating it" assertion

render.states: render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies
render.because: Base UI's render prop takes an element or a function of the list's own state, so its type is a union of a React element and a callback - neither expressible in JSON Schema.

style.states: style accepts a function of the list's state as well as a plain style object
style.because: Base UI widens React's `CSSProperties` to `CSSProperties | ((state) => CSSProperties)` so a caller can style off the primitive's own state (orientation, tabActivationDirection). A JSON Schema `object` would reject the function form, so nothing is asserted; the kit's own styling goes through tabs.module.css, not through this.

unexposed_parts.reason: TabsList renders exactly one Tabs.Indicator itself, right after its children, to draw the single bar that travels to the active trigger under the `line` variant; there is no exported part for it, and a list never holds more than one. The `default` variant marks its active trigger with a fill and a hairline instead and draws no bar at all.

good.title: A list of two triggers, default variant
A flat, line-variant list at the small size

bad.title: A TabsList with no Tabs root around it
bad.why: TabsList reads and writes the nearest Tabs root's state through Base UI context; outside one, its triggers have no shared value to select or report.

render.description: TS: ReactElement<unknown, string | JSXElementConstructor<any>> | ComponentRenderFn<HTMLProps, TabsListState> | undefined. The compiler emits one JSON type per property; this type is left to tsc. render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies. Base UI's render prop takes an element or a function of the list's own state, so its type is a union of a React element and a callback - neither expressible in JSON Schema.

style.description: TS: CSSProperties | ((state: TabsListState) => CSSProperties | undefined) | undefined. The compiler emits one JSON type per property; this type is left to tsc. style accepts a function of the list's state as well as a plain style object. Base UI widens React's `CSSProperties` to `CSSProperties | ((state) => CSSProperties)` so a caller can style off the primitive's own state (orientation, tabActivationDirection). A JSON Schema `object` would reject the function form, so nothing is asserted; the kit's own styling goes through tabs.module.css, not through this.
